concepts.angle: Paint each edge with one of k colors so every color class is a spanning tree; K4 with k=2 succeeds and is exactly tight (6 = 2*3) while Petersen fails, and the failure hands you a one-line partition certificate — making concrete that the ONLY obstruction to packing k spanning trees is a clustering of the vertices whose k(r-1) toll cannot be paid.

Sweep the clustering resolution r from 2 to n and compare the exact minimum cross-edge count against the toll k(r-1): three K5 islands joined by three single bridges pass the cut test (r=2) AND the headcount test (r=n) yet fail at r=3, proving that the Nash-Williams-Tutte condition genuinely quantifies over every partition because sparsity can hide at an intermediate resolution — then 2k-edge-connectivity is shown to be the cheap sufficient condition via double counting.

Contraction as a physical camera: the user drags vertices into blobs and pulls the camera back until each blob collapses to a supernode, so that a pre-verified packing of k edge-disjoint spanning trees is seen leaving behind at least r-1 cross edges per colour (each tree's image is a connected spanning submultigraph of G/P, never necessarily a tree), which sums by edge-disjointness to the partition condition e_G(P) >= k(r-1) — the necessity half proved in the user's hands, plus the connected-parts reduction discovered by building a deliberately disconnected part, and an explicit refusal to claim the converse.

The hard direction of Nash-Williams–Tutte as a good characterisation (TONCAS): a real k-forest packing algorithm runs live, greedily grows, runs a breadth-first exchange/augmenting search over EDGES when an edge fits nowhere, applies swap chains end-first — and when the search finally closes with nothing found, the set A of edges it reached is collapsed into the partition P = components of (V,A), whose cross-edge count is then recounted from scratch by a verifier sharing no code with the solver and shown to fall below k(r-1). The user watches an algorithm's failure turn into a short, independently checkable proof of impossibility, and lands on the dichotomy: either k labelled spanning trees or one sparse partition, never neither and never both, both witnesses polynomially checkable.

Nash-Williams–Tutte as ONE continuous family of tests indexed by resolution: a 3-D tower holds every partition-size r at once — level r is the quotient graph after clustering V into r parts, trunks are the nesting relation, and a budget ladder beside it draws e_G(P) against the toll k(r-1) at every level; because the toll is linear in r the ladder's toll ticks form a straight dashed line while the cross counts form a rising curve, so the tower's SIDE FACE is literally the f(r) vs k(r-1) chart while its TOP VIEW is the graph collapsing into clusters. Scrolling descends the tower. The payload is that r=2 (k-edge-connectivity) and r=n (|E| >= k(n-1)) are merely the bottom and top of that one continuum, that neither endpoint nor both together suffice, and that a graph can be sparse only at an intermediate scale — demonstrated by four presets that fail at the coarse end only, the fine end only, the middle only, and nowhere.

roles_by_concept.01-color-the-trees: renders every mathematical statement on the page: the iff-statement in the hero, the tight budget identity |E(K4)| = k(n-1), the Petersen certificate 15 < 2*(10-1), the contraction/toll implication chain, the 3xK5 intermediate-partition inequality, the boxed final theorem, and the 2k-edge-connectivity corollary
roles_by_concept.02-hidden-resolution: renders the iff-statement of the theorem, the contraction/toll implication chain T -> T/P -> >= r-1, the r=2 specialisation to k-edge-connectivity, the r=n headcount, the 2k-edge-connectivity corollary, the double-counting line e_G(P) = 1/2 sum |delta(V_i)| >= kr > k(r-1), and the closing min-over-partitions restatement
roles_by_concept.03-contract-and-count: all notation: the iff statement of the theorem with the definition of e_G(P), the definition of a packing, the three-line necessity chain (T_i connected -> T_i/P connected on r supernodes -> |T_i n E(P)| >= r-1), the summation line e_G(P) = |E(P)| >= sum |T_i n E(P)| >= k(r-1) where edge-disjointness is spent, the connected-parts reduction as an aligned block (e_G(P')=e_G(P), r'=r+j-1 => k(r'-1)>k(r-1)), the contrapositive for the 3xK5 certificate, and both directions of the theorem side by side in the honesty section. Rendered by a single [data-tex]/[data-tex-d] sweep with throwOnError:false.
roles_by_concept.04-certificate-duality: all notation, via one [data-tex] (inline) / [data-tex-d] (display) sweep with throwOnError:false and an idempotence guard. Renders: the theorem as an iff with \underbrace-labelled 'witness A' / 'no witness B exists' halves, the definition of e_G(P), the toll k(r-1) decomposed by \underbrace into trees x welds, the three-line necessity chain, the quoted exchange identity sum|F_i| = (|E|-|A|) + k(n-c(A)), its rearrangement into |E|-|A| < k(r-1), and the O(|E| alpha) / O(|E|) checking costs on the two dichotomy cards. All 20 .woff2 faces vendored.
roles_by_concept.05-glue-budget: all notation, via one [data-tex] (inline) / [data-tex-d] (display) sweep with throwOnError:false and a data-done idempotence guard, plus imperative katex.render calls for the two live statements that change on every interaction (the toll k(r-1)=k*(r-1)=N, and the level inequality e_G(P)=X >= or < k(r-1)=Y). Renders the theorem as an iff, the definition of e_G(P), the two-line necessity chain with the sum over T_i, the two endpoint identities (min over |P|=2 <=> lambda(G) >= k, and e_G(P)=|E| >= k(n-1)), the monotonicity f(r-1) <= f(r), and the max-packing formula min floor(f(r)/(r-1)). All 20 .woff2 faces vendored.

roles_by_concept.04-certificate-duality: the only animation engine. (1) The §3 flood: anime.timeline() with a shared `update` callback chaining four tweens on a plain state object {t, shown} — reached-set highlight, blob hardening (t drives both the Minkowski pad and the interior-edge opacity), cross-edge reveal, then a round:1 count-in of cross edges — writing back into the 'harden' range input each frame so the manual slider and the playback are the same control. (2) The §1 weld arcs staggered in by (treeIndex*(r-1)+weldIndex)*55ms. (3) A short opacity pulse on the main SVG at every swap/found step. Chosen over GSAP (claimed by artifact 03) and over d3.transition (would duplicate D3's job).

roles_by_concept.05-glue-budget: the one statistical panel (§4): a mixed scatter+line chart carrying the partition CLOUD (one bubble per distinct (r, e(P)) with radius scaled by log of how many partitions share it — up to 678,570 partitions binned for the exhaustive graphs, a stated 40,000-partition sample otherwise), the true minimum f(r) as a line, the tower's nested chain as a dashed line, the toll k(r-1) as a neutral dashed reference line, and failing resolutions as oversized crossRot status markers. Supplies the axes, legend, and a custom tooltip that reports partition counts. A different job from Three (chart vs scene), so no overlap; D3/ECharts/Paper.js/Cytoscape are claimed by artifacts 01-04.

roles_by_concept.02-hidden-resolution: renders every clustered graph view: a partition is drawn as cytoscape COMPOUND PARENT NODES (one labelled box per part) with the vertices at hand-authored preset positions, re-clustering is node.move({parent}) plus empty-parent removal, cross vs internal edges are edge classes recoloured on every change, click-to-recluster is a tap handler on node.v, and the contracted quotient multigraph G/P is a second instance using curve-style:bezier so parallel cross edges fan out

roles_by_concept.04-certificate-duality: the only DOM/data-join layer. Every SVG scene is a pure function of a step snapshot re-rendered through selection.join with stable keys: edges keyed by edge index (stroke = forest colour, stroke-dasharray = forest dash, a separate low-alpha halo layer for 'reached by the search' and a stronger one for the F_i-cycle currently being walked), vertices keyed by vertex id, partition blobs keyed by part id, and the BFS search structure keyed by edge id. Also supplies d3.polygonHull (input to the rounded-hull blob path), d3.line().curve(d3.curveCatmullRom.alpha(0.6)) for the augmenting-chain overlay through edge midpoints, d3.group for BFS depth rows, d3.range/d3.mean, and the survey/brute-force table joins. d3.transition is DELIBERATELY UNUSED so it never overlaps Anime.js.

roles_by_concept.02-hidden-resolution: the centrepiece resolution-scan chart (two stacked grids sharing one category axis r: bars of exact minimum cross edges + dashed toll line k(r-1) on top, diverging slack bars below, linked axisPointer, per-item status colours, a markPoint annotating only the FIRST failing r, and a click handler that loads that r's minimising partition into the graph); also the live toll meters (horizontal 2-bar comparison of cross edges vs toll) and the 1-bridge-vs-2-bridges comparison line chart

roles_by_concept.03-contract-and-count: the two timelines. (1) The camera tween: gsap.to(state, {t:0->1, duration:0.95, ease:'power2.inOut', onUpdate:draw}) driven by the contract/expand buttons and mirrored back into the range input; touching the canvas while t>0 fires the reverse tween instead of starting a drag. (2) The weld playback: a monotone gsap.to on a scalar whose onUpdate ceils to an integer reveal count, stepping one colour's surviving edges into the quotient one at a time (duration scales with the edge count) and re-running the union-find replay on each step. Killed and restarted whenever the user grabs the reveal slider.

every canvas on the page, via one paper.PaperScope per <canvas> (paper-core, not paper-full — PaperScript is unused). Draws: organic part blobs as round-join outward offsets of a monotone-chain convex hull fed through Path.smooth({type:'continuous'}); cross edges as Path.quadraticCurveTo whose perpendicular control offset is (fanIndex - (m-1)/2) * FAN * smoothstep(t), so parallel quotient edges physically fan apart as the contraction proceeds and are countable at t=1; interior edges as dashed lines whose opacity dissolves to 0 by t=0.55; supernodes as circles whose radius grows with part size and whose alpha follows smoothstep(0.30,0.86,t); the lasso as a live open path plus a translucent closed twin; and PointText labels for vertices, part letters and loop-deletion badges. Whole scene is cleared and rebuilt with project.clear() on every frame — the drawing is a pure function of (positions, part map, t). Also supplies view.viewToProject for pointer hit-testing and view.zoom/view.center for fitting a logical coordinate box to any canvas size.

roles_by_concept.05-glue-budget: the only spatial engine, driving all three scenes. (1) THE TOWER: for r = 2..n a Group per level holding cluster spheres (radius 0.042+0.050*sqrt(|part|), colour = a low-chroma identity ramp keyed to the cluster's minimum member index so an island keeps its hue as it forms), quotient cross edges as oriented cylinders with a lateral fan offset per parallel edge, a rung to the ladder, a cross-count bar, a hatched shortfall segment, a toll tick, a red RingGeometry halo on failing levels, and a canvas-texture Sprite 'r=..'; plus trunk cylinders to the next coarser level (chain mode only), two polylines (Line for the e(P) profile, LineDashedMaterial + computeLineDistances for the straight k(r-1) toll line) and a live readout Sprite redrawn on focus change. Focus is expressed purely as per-level material opacity (1.0 vs 0.20) plus lazily built 'focus extras' — original vertex dots, faint interior edges, and RingGeometry cluster hulls for parts of size >= 2. (2) §1 TOLL WIDGET: r cluster spheres on a ring and k stars of r-1 QuadraticBezierCurve3 weld arcs, each tree bowed to its own height. (3) §5 TREES: the wiring at y=0 and one Group per spanning tree, separated purely by group.position.y so the peel slider never rebuilds geometry. Chosen because the stack-of-resolutions IS a spatial object with two meaningful projections; flattening it would need three separate 2-D pictures.

orbit + dolly + damping for all three scenes, attached per renderer with enableDamping and per-scene min/max distance; enablePan only on the tower and the tree stack. Programmatic camera presets are tweened by lerping camera.position and controls.target together in the rAF loop, then handed back to the controls. Vendored from three 0.137.5 because r149 deleted examples/js entirely; it touches only stable core APIs (Vector3, Quaternion, Spherical, EventDispatcher, MOUSE, TOUCH) and runs unchanged against r149.
